description: Autofill matching: URI preparation with the scheme prefix, trim, user information, and empty-label rules, cross-site lookalikes, page URLs, registrable domains with the known_suffixes table, every match mode, the scheme rule and local hosts, item outcomes and candidate order, frame selection, and save offers. Expected values are worked out from the spec text by hand. The known-suffix lookup returns the longest entry of known_suffixes that equals the host or a sequence of its trailing labels, except that suffix_answers replaces the answer for the hosts it lists; each of those answers fails the check, so a registrable result is null and every match involving such a host is none. Items are compact: a client expands each into a full body item with these values. Hosts and origins are serialised as WHATWG URLs write them, with one trailing dot of a domain removed. The known_suffixes table is a fixture: a few real Public Suffix List rules, home.arpa included, not the whole list. Android cases: android_page builds the Android web page <scheme>://<host>/ from a browser's scheme and host, android_match, android_items, and android_save match it, and app_items, app_bind, and app_save use an app page {package, signers, history (oldest first), multiple_signers} with digests in lowercase hex. A compact item's optional apps lists its login.apps entries. app_items gives each candidate's kind; app_bind gives the item's login.apps after a confirmed fill, or null when the fill records nothing; a new item in an android_save or app_save result lists its uris and apps.
